items.title: Man City dump Brighton out of Carabao Cup after shoot-out victory
items.excerpt: Carabao Cup holders Manchester City needed penalties to progress past Brighton and into the quarter-finals after battling from behind to draw the game 2-2 at the Etihad.
body: Carabao Cup holders Manchester City needed penalties to progress past Brighton and into the quarter-finals after battling from behind to draw the game 2-2 at the Etihad.

Enzo Maresca's side never led on the night but scored four of their five penalties to win the deciding shoot-out 4-3, with Rayan Cherki striking the winner and Geronimo Rulli denying both Yasin Ayari and Lewis Dunk.

Brighton, the better side for the majority, will consider themselves unlucky to be dumped out of a competition Fabian Hurzeler had earlier professed to want to win. But City stuck to task and eventually prevailed on penalties - Hurzeler gets his chance to enact revenge when the two sides meet again in the Premier League on Saturday. items.title: Ref Watch: Arsenal's red card appeal will fail - Dowman was aggressive
items.excerpt: Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher believes Arsenal's appeal against Max Dowman's red card in their shock Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town will fail.
body: Former Premier League referee Dermot Gallagher believes Arsenal's appeal against Max Dowman's red card in their shock Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town will fail.
Dowman was sent off for violent conduct after kicking out at Harrison Neal following the defender's strong challenge on the teenager late in the fourth-round tie, which Arsenal lost on penalties.
Arsenal must submit appeal documents by 1pm on Thursday and are hopeful a decision will be made before their match at Liverpool, live on Sky Sports on Sunday.

However, when asked if he thought Arsenal's appeal would be successful, Gallagher told Sky Sports News : "I don't, because of the aggressiveness of Dowman, and you can see the intent. I think it will fail." items.title: Carrick and Fernandes hold clear-the-air talks ahead of Chelsea fixture
items.excerpt: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick and captain Bruno Fernandes have met face to face to clear the air, with both vowing to refocus on turning the club's season around.
body: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick and captain Bruno Fernandes have met face to face to clear the air, with both vowing to refocus on turning the club's season around.

Fernandes was an unused substitute after being dropped for the 3-0 defeat against Bournemouth on Sunday after he criticised Carrick's tactics following the 4-1 thrashing at Como in the Champions League.
Carrick had described his reasons for dropping his captain as "pure football".

"Picking the team is always a difficult decision," Carrick told Sky Sports . "We've got to make what we feel is the right one for the team to try to get the performance we want." items.title: Arteta explains reaction to Dowman red card amid criticism
items.excerpt: Mikel Arteta has explained his reaction to Max Dowman as the 16-year-old went down the tunnel after being sent off in Arsenal's shock Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood Town.
body: Mikel Arteta has explained his reaction to Max Dowman as the 16-year-old went down the tunnel after being sent off in Arsenal's shock Carabao Cup exit to Fleetwood Town.

Moments before Arsenal exited the competition on penalties to the League Two side, Dowman was sent off for violent conduct for kicking out at Harrison Neal after the Fleetwood defender's strong challenge on the teenager.

As Dowman headed towards the tunnel and past the dugouts, Arteta leaned in and said something to the teenager, which Paul Merson criticised, saying the Arsenal manager should have put an arm around him. items.title: Sunderland's first-half blitz sends them past Brentford into quarters
items.excerpt: Three goals in 13 first-half minutes saw Sunderland blitz past Brentford and into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals with a 3-2 win at the Stadium of Light.
body: Three goals in 13 first-half minutes saw Sunderland blitz past Brentford and into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals with a 3-2 win at the Stadium of Light.

The Black Cats owed much to 21-year-old Jocelin Ta Bi for his trio of assists to turn the game on its head after Brentford had dominated the early stages - and hit the post, bar and saw a shot cleared off the line in one move at 0-0.

Ta Bi, who joined Sunderland in January but had only featured four times since, was a livewire on the right flank in that first 45 minutes and thought he had opened his account for the club with a low drive that beat Hakon Valdimarsson, only for Chemsdine Talbi to tap home on the line and claim the goal.
